public_rationale: Within the claimed period, products gained material new workflows: desktop interaction through Claude and document-based audio discussions through NotebookLM. An independent case study corroborates the desktop capability. These developments contradict the ordinary capability-based reading of products being trapped in amber. They do not settle the separate judgment that no product was important enough to justify the industry's investment.
limitations: Meaningful progress requires an evaluator judgment.
Computer use remained an experimental beta.
The independent computer-use evidence is a preliminary case study.
Feature availability does not establish commercial success or high reliability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI products have not meaningfully progressed for over a year.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI's products have effectively been trapped in amber for over a year.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that available products had made no material progress in user capabilities or workflows.
I examine the final full year before publication. Material progress within that year contradicts stagnation lasting more than a year, even though the earlier starting point is unspecified.
A meaningful change enables a substantively different task or interaction. A new model name or a small benchmark gain alone is insufficient.
The neighboring claim about industry-defining importance is stronger and more subjective than the product-stagnation claim assessed here.
criteria.support_condition: Available products during the year show only minor refinements, with no demonstrated material additions to what users can do.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Products released during the year demonstrate material new capabilities or workflows that users or developers could actually access.

evidence.explanation: Developers could use the API to have Claude inspect screens, move a cursor, click and type. This materially extends possible workflows, although Anthropic describes the release as experimental and error-prone.

Researchers independently examined the released product on desktop tasks, corroborating that computer interaction was an observable capability. This preliminary case study does not establish reliable general automation.
